brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.requirement: Tool rack that hangs on wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: Three cells (piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) in row with keyhole hangers on back: accessory:0#-1,0#3 and accessory:0#0,0#2 (rear slots) plus accessory:0#1,0#2 demonstrates wall-mount pattern. Hangers accept screw heads in wall for lift-and-drop mounting.

Four hook plates installed: accessory:0#-1,0#1, accessory:0#0,0#1, accessory:0#0,0#4, accessory:0#1,0#2 - each plate carries two hooks, distributed across rack front/sides to hang hand tools. Compatible props are cable coil, gaffer tape roll or FPV goggles per configurator.

finish.summary: Built 3-cell linear rack ( -1,0 + 0,0 + 1,0 ) with keyhole hangers on rear faces for wall mounting and four hook plates on front/side faces for small hand tools. Capped open ends and locked joints. Staging props demonstrated the limitation that hooks sit low relative to bench height in the configurator view.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
